decisions.issues: Minor only. The coat shows a wet sheen but is not clearly soaked dark at the shoulders. Two turbaned gate guards with spears have been added; they are harmless background. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch25 uniform: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, talwar and buckled boots. The bay mare has black points and no white markings, so she reads as Kayal. The rainy grey sky at upper left is clear for both captions.

Minor only. Nagoji stands just inside the open door rather than in the doorway itself. He is seen from behind with his profile visible: clean chin, moustache, ear stud, topknot and grey temple all read. Water drips from his hands, which matches 'shaking rain from his sleeves'. The red waistcoat reads more like a sash from behind. The floor plan matches the script: Ramayyan cross-legged on a low seat under the barred window with the neem tree in rain behind him, the lamp niche on the side wall, a low table with palm-leaf bundles, and the empty stool facing him. Plain wall left of the window and right of it above the niche gives room for both balloons.

Minor floor-plan drift: a second barred window is painted on the door-side wall facing Ramayyan (the script's one window should be behind him, as in 1.4), and the lamp niche sits on his left rather than his right. Otherwise clean: over-Ramayyan's-shoulder framing, Nagoji dripping in the doorway in the white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain and topknot with grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud; empty stool waiting; palm leaf weighted by a river stone with no script; Ramayyan's hand resting on his knee away from it. Balloon space: clear whitewashed wall between the window and Nagoji (x 0.46-0.64, y 0.02-0.45) or above the window. Ramayyan is seen from behind, so his tail points at the side of his head.

Minor: Ramayyan sits on a floor mat, not a low wooden seat; the stool is plain wood where 1.3 shows a rush seat; the table has turned legs; there is faint stubble shading on Nagoji's jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. Otherwise the beat is right: Nagoji on the stool with his wet coat dripping onto the stone floor, and Ramayyan lifting the river stone, with the palm leaf showing no script. The room matches the floor plan, with the barred window and neem behind Ramayyan, the niche lamp to his side and the open door with rain behind Nagoji. Both faces match their sheets; the ear stud is small and gold. Balloon space: the rain and door at upper left, the wall column between Nagoji's head and the window (x 0.37-0.5), and the wall above Ramayyan's head (x 0.74-0.92, y 0-0.2).

Minor only. There is light stipple shading on the chin and jaw, but no beard; the chin reads as clean at print size. The leaf is a bit thick and board-like, but only its blank back faces the reader, so no script shows. The brand on the inner left wrist is a blurred shapeless patch beside a white scar, sitting just below the cuff rather than a hand's width up. The room is slightly re-arranged: the barred window and lamp niche sit behind Nagoji, with the door at left. Lighting, costume and props are consistent with the page. Plain wall at upper left, between the door and his head, and right of the window above the niche gives room for both captions.

Soft beat miss. Nagoji's hands are clasped over his knee and there is no leaf in his hands, even though he holds it in 1.5 and again in 2.4. The framing is a full-figure two-shot, wider than the scripted medium, and it nearly repeats 1.4. Everything else is clean. The room matches page 1 (door behind the stool, barred window onto the neem in the rain, brass niche lamp to Ramayyan's right, low table with palm-leaf bundles). Nagoji is on model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain. Ramayyan is on model and unhurried, with stylus and bundle. Eyelines meet, hands are sound, and the art has no text. There is clear wall space top-left for Nagoji's balloon and top-right for Ramayyan's long one.

Minor only: a few small palm trees stand among the trees behind the ramparts, although the setting asked for no coconut palms. They read as inland greenery, not coast. Chanda Sahib is solid rather than notably heavy. Otherwise clean. The captive matches his description: white Mughal jama, high cream turban, beard seen only from behind in partial profile, no readable face and no red. His wrists are chained behind his back, with chains running to the riders ahead and behind. White-clad Maratha horsemen under saffron swallow-tailed pennants surround him and lead him away from the Tiruchirappalli walls, rock and summit temple, at a distance in cool, dusty daylight. There is no painted text, blood or anachronism, and the horse anatomy is sound. Clear open sky across the upper left and centre (about x 0 to 0.7, y 0 to 0.27) gives room for both captions.

Minor issues only. The shot shows the face down to the moustache above the leaf, a little wider than eyes and brow. The background shows the barred window and an empty low bench behind Nagoji rather than a purely bare wall. This matches the reverse angle already used in 1.5. Nagoji is on model: thick curled moustache, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, coat, waistcoat and chain. The leaf is seen from the back with no script, and his hands are sound. The brass open-wick niche lamp warms the wall. The upper wall above and right of his head gives room for the three letter captions.

Minor issues only. Young Nagoji's turban is a deep orange-red, closer to rust than the scripted dusty saffron, and he wears a red sash. This is consistent with the bible's pre-capture memory dress. One small background attendant at lower right has a beard. The principals match: the sardar is on the left, older, heavy-jowled, with a grey-streaked moustache, clean chin, jewelled turban ornament and brocade angarkha, and his hand is clapped on Nagoji's shoulder. Young Nagoji has no grey, a clean chin, moustache, gold stud and talwar, and is grinning. The brown marks on his angarkha read as dust, not blood. The panel has horses, saffron pennants and no text. The sky top-centre and top-right and the tree canopy top-left hold the three lettering items without covering faces.

Minor only. Nagoji's stool is a chair-height rush stool rather than the low stool of the floor plan (it matches 3.2). The leaf he puts down is a small tied bundle rather than a single leaf. There is light stubble shading on the chin, which is within tolerance. Otherwise it is on model: uniform, silver chain, topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin and gold stud, with the scar on the left forearm as the ch25 row allows. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The room matches 1.2 to 2.1: door behind Nagoji, barred window onto the neem in rain, lamp niche. There is open wall below the window and at upper right for both balloons.

Minor: light stubble-like hatching on the chin and jaw, but it reads as shading, not a beard. Otherwise on model: thick curled moustache, small flush gold ear stud, topknot with grey at the temples, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain of office. The medallions on the chain are ornamental, with no pseudo-text. He has the wary side-glance the beat needs. The door behind him fits the floor plan, since the stool has the door behind it. The plain plaster wall at upper right (x 0.62-1.0, y 0-0.6) has room for both balloons. Ramayyan's off-panel balloon tails to the right edge, where Nagoji is looking.

Minor: he sits upright and cross-legged rather than visibly leaning back, but his hands rest lightly on his knees as scripted and both hands are well drawn. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding curly hair, bare-headed, plain white cloth, no marks or jewellery. The setting matches the floor plan. The barred window is unglazed, with the neem and rain outside only. The clay niche lamp is on his right, and the low table holds palm-leaf bundles and a stylus, with no script on them. Plain whitewashed wall at upper right (x 0.74-0.98, y 0.02-0.48) and between the niche and the window gives room for both balloons.

Minor. The intercepted ola is drawn as a squarish folded leaf with string holes and faint horizontal ribs, not a long narrow strip. It shows no glyphs, so there is no legible or pseudo script. The hanging lamp is an open-wick brass hanging lamp on rods, not a glass lantern. Otherwise the scripted beat is all there: a soft-edged cutaway of a toll post in rain on the road, a plain unlettered flag, the barrier, the pack horse with its saddlebags open, a clerk in plain cotton reading the leaf under the eaves, and the trader haggling with a second clerk over cloth bales. A large clear sky across the top takes both off-panel balloons, whose tails run to the top edge toward the room panels.

Minor. A cluster of unscripted round hanging objects beside the window reads as dried gourds (the teal one is slightly glossy). A second plank door appears further along the courtyard wall. Otherwise it matches the script: an exterior seen from the narrow courtyard in the storm, rain driving and water sheeting off the tiled eaves and down the weathered wall, the neem streaming, and a single small barred window glowing with lamplight and no figures. There is enough low-detail space for three balloons on the wall left of the window, the courtyard wall and the wet paving.

Clean. The father matches the bible: white-haired, bent, white pheta, black wool kambal and coarse dhoti, with a hand on his lower back as he straightens. The brother's wife ladles ghee at the hearth, the two nephews are in new cloth, and the light is warm on black-soil Deccan fields with a hill fort behind. Edges are crisper than 'soft-edged like memory', but that is a minor style note. No text. Hands are sound. Open sky at top centre (x 0.35-0.6, y 0.03-0.2) takes the caption.

Acceptable with minor notes. The captured laterite bastion fort flies saffron swallow-tailed pennants, Maratha horse in cream angarkhas and white pagdis pour down the ghat road past the gate, European ships sit offshore, and the light is cold and grey. The guns point at the village by the river, but that village lies between the fort and the sea, so the guns face seaward and 'swung round to point inland' reads only loosely. The ships are too small for men at the rails to show. No text and no redcoats. Wide open grey sky across the top takes the caption.

Clean. Pepper vines with green spikes climb a jackfruit tree in the foreground, a Kerala estate house burns, and Maratha riders with a saffron swallow-tailed pennant are silhouetted against the flames. It is night, with no bodies and no text. The frame is 3:2 landscape for a half-tier panel, so a narrower crop should keep the riders and the burning house (centre and right). Dark sky at upper right (x 0.55-0.85, y 0.02-0.2) takes the caption.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet and the ch20-28 row: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, bell earrings, bead necklace, armlet, a tali pendant, grey threading in her hair and a faint sandalwood line at the hairline. She grips the wooden bars of an unglazed window at dusk, watching smoke and fire on the horizon. The brass lamps have open wicks. The hand is sound and there is no text. Dusk sky at upper right (x 0.55-0.85, y 0.03-0.25) takes the caption. The frame is 3:2 landscape for a half-tier panel; a crop should keep her face and the smoke.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the ch25-27 row: white European coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain of office, breeches, riding boots, topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache and a gold ear stud. His palm lies flat on the single leaf. One minor point: a faint stipple of stubble under his lower lip; the chin still reads as clean-shaven at print size. Ramayyan matches his sheet, holding a stylus with one hand on his bundles, and looks skeptical. The room matches page 1 panel 4: door behind Nagoji, barred window onto the neem in the rain, and the lamp niche on the right wall. Ramayyan sits on a backed chair rather than cross-legged on a low seat, as in pages 1 and 3. No text on the leaf (only specks). All hands are sound. For five lines: a wide clear wall between the figures below the window (x 0.38-0.62, y 0.38-0.72), wall left of the window (x 0.33-0.4, y 0.02-0.35), and wall above and right of Ramayyan's head (x 0.62-0.68 and 0.78-0.86, y 0.0-0.14).

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin sharp features, receding curly hair, plain unbordered white cloth, no marks. He leans forward over the table, eyes narrowed at the viewer (Nagoji), hands flat beside the leaf weighted by the river stone. No stool is visible, the barred window with the neem in rain is behind him, and there is no text in the art. A small nit: the niche lamp is at frame right, which is his left, but that matches the accepted page 4.5 and 6.1 two-shots. The plain wall between his head and the niche (x 0.55-0.83, y 0.02-0.35) takes the balloon.

Acceptable. This is the scripted head-and-shoulders close-up. Nagoji has his topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a tiny flush gold stud, the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Behind him is the door wall, with no window. He is lit warm from the niche lamp at right, with catchlights in his eyes, and both hands and forearms are out of frame. One small reservation: faint stipple shading on the jaw and chin. At page size it reads as clean-shaven, and it is far lighter than the rejected v01. Ramayyan is off-panel to the right, where Nagoji is looking, so both tails go to the right edge. The plain wall at upper right (x 0.5-0.84, y 0.0-0.5) takes both balloons.

Acceptable insert, with minor flaws. Ramayyan's hand reads broad and veined rather than thin. The single Deccan leaf under its stone is not shown as the target. The barred window sits across the room rather than behind Ramayyan. An empty rush stool stands against the far wall, but it reads as spare furniture, not as Nagoji's seat. The beat is clear: his bare forearm and white cloth come in from the top left, sliding a blank leaf and an iron stylus across the table. The leaf is blank, with only a string hole. There is no text, and the anatomy is sound. Clear wall space for both balloons: the upper right (x 0.78-0.92, y 0.0-0.4) and the middle wall (x 0.45-0.68, y 0.28-0.55). Ramayyan's head is just off the top-left edge.

Acceptable with reservations. The framing is a medium shot that takes in Nagoji's downturned face and the room, not the scripted tight insert on the hands. The hands are still the clear focus. His right fist grips the iron stylus like a sword hilt. His left hand cradles the blank leaf palm-up with the white cuff slid back. On the inner left forearm near the wrist, the brand is now an irregular, puckered pale patch with no letters and no cross, and a thin white scar runs toward the elbow, which fixes the r1 failure. Both hands are well formed with five fingers each. The face fits his look: topknot hair, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold stud, smooth jaw. The background has a backed bench under the window and a stool at right. That bends the no-chairs floor plan, but it matches the already accepted 5.3. There is no text in the art. The caption fits on the plain wall between the window and the niche (x 0.62-0.85, y 0.0-0.35).

Acceptable. Padmini now matches her sheet: heavy-set, stern, square-jawed, thick curly black hair with no grey, gold earrings and bead necklace, cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no blouse. She hands a brass cup under the jackfruit tree to young Nagoji, seen from behind. The other fragments all read: the bangled, turmeric-stained hands tying a black thread (hands only), the thin hand slipping by the rope in the storm sea, and the small spyglass boy against the sky, all flowing out of the lamplight as smoke. Nagoji at the table is correct: topknot, grey temples, moustache, small gold stud, coat sleeves to the wrist with no brand showing, stylus moving on the leaf. Minor points: the boy's platform is on stilts beside a palm, not on a palm top; the drowning wrist shows no rag cuff; and there is an extra clay lamp on the table besides the niche lamp. There is no text in the art. The caption fits on the plain lower-left wall (x 0.02-0.2, y 0.5-0.78).

Minor: Ramayyan sits on a stool beside the table's far end, not right under the window, so the floor plan is only loosely kept, as it is across the rest of the page. Nagoji's far foot under the table looks like a low shoe rather than a riding boot. Some Nair soldiers in the inset wear red turbans. Faces, ear stud, clean chin, forearm scar, stylus hand, plain flags and Dutch tricorn square are all correct. There is no painted text. Captions fit at top-left over the door and tree and on the wall above the window, left of the inset.

Clean. The angular laterite bastion carries a battery of guns, and masons on bamboo scaffolding patch the wall below. The left half is darkened as if a hand had passed across it. The caption can sit in the dark sky at upper left. The workers' faces are tiny and well away from that space.

Acceptable. A Maratha sardar (white pagdi and angarkha) and a Nair chief (topknot, bare chest, white gold-bordered mundu, gold earrings) sit as equals on a tiled verandah, with a brass betel box between them. Closed tribute chests are pushed back into the dark half at left. Minor: the Nair chief wears a thin white cord across his chest that may read as a sacred thread, which is unusual for a Nair. The shadow is drawn as a dark interior rather than 6.2's soft gradient, but it carries the same idea. Captions fit in the dark upper-left area and in the sky at upper right.

Acceptable, with minor notes. It is the same room as the rest of the page. Ramayyan matches his sheet and reads the leaf intently, and Nagoji is correct for chapter 25 (uniform, chain, topknot, gold stud, clean chin). Minor: Nagoji kneads his LEFT (branded) forearm and hand with his right hand, but the writing hand set up in 5.4 and 5.5 is the right. The brand is drawn as a faint circular seal ring, not a pale puckered patch, though it has no letters and is not a cross. Ramayyan's two balloons fit over the rain window and the plain wall below it, with tails to his mouth at upper right.

Minor: Nagoji sits with the barred window and a bench behind him, which reads more like Ramayyan's side of the room, though the open rainy door and the niche lamp match 6.1. The ear studs are tiny and pale but are studs with nothing hanging. The chin is clean with light stubble shading. Hands clasped on the table are sound, and the scar is on the left forearm. There is no text. Balloons fit on the plain wall left of his head (x 0.2-0.42, upper half) and on the wall below the window (x 0.6-0.78, y 0.4-0.6).

Minor only. Ramayyan's fingertips rest lightly on the tied leaf bundle when the script has his hands off it, so it reads as him just setting it down. He is drawn still rather than visibly nodding. The 'read leaf' is a tied bundle rather than a single leaf. Otherwise clean. The room matches page 6 (door left, barred window centre with rain outside only, lamp niche right) and both men match their sheets: Nagoji in full ch25 uniform with topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud and a pale scar on the left forearm. Clear wall space sits between the figures under the window and to the right of the window above Ramayyan for the three balloons.

Matches the tight insert. Nagoji's hand, with ridged nails and the white coat cuff with its brass button, comes down from the left and pins Ramayyan's thin bare wrist and hand, with the edge of his white cloth showing, on the leaf bundle. Both hands are anatomically plausible. There is no text, and the lamp is a clay one in the side niche. The dark wall at upper centre leaves clean space for NAGOJI's 'No.'. Nagoji is off-panel to the upper left, so the tail goes to the left edge near the top. Minor: both hands are drawn quite old and wrinkled.

Minor only. Three hands crowd the table centre: Ramayyan's free hand rests beside the one Nagoji covers. The anatomy holds and the beat reads clearly. There is light stipple shading on Nagoji's cheek, but the chin reads clean. The room and seating match 7.1 (Nagoji left on his stool by the door, Ramayyan right, window behind, lamp niche right). Ramayyan looks up with his brows raised. Nagoji's long balloon will need to sit high, over the upper window and wall between the two heads or above the door at upper left. 'Yes.' fits on the plain wall right of Ramayyan's head.

A quiet close-up on Nagoji that matches his sheet and the chapter 25 row. He has a thick curled moustache, a small flush gold ear stud, a topknot with grey at the temples, the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, and no turban. The closed door with its ring handle sits behind his stool, so the floor plan holds. Plain wall at upper right and upper left gives room for both balloons. Minor: faint stubble stippling on the chin and jaw. It reads as clean-shaven at panel size, but it is not perfectly smooth.

Matches the beat. Nagoji stands at the side-wall lamp niche holding two leaves with their tips at the flame, and Ramayyan sits behind him on his low seat under the barred window, watching. The table, the leaves and the stool by the door all keep the floor plan. Both characters match their sheets. There is no text, and the hands are sound. Clear wall between the window and Nagoji takes RAMAYYAN's balloon. Minor points: (1) Ramayyan faces forward and watches with only his eyes rather than turning on his seat. (2) The door stands open onto a rainy courtyard with wet stone at the threshold, while panel 4 shows it closed. (3) The niche lamp is brass here but clay in panel 2; both materials are allowed. (4) Light stubble texture on Nagoji's jaw. (5) He wears a leather waist belt with a buckle, which suits the period.

Acceptable. A tight profile of Nagoji facing right toward the clay lamp in the niche, eyes on the flame. Thick curled moustache, smooth clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey at the temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain all match. The rainy barred window matches 7.5. Minor: the two leaves carry faint dotted rows of pseudo-script that show only at full zoom and disappear at inset print size; retouch them blank if possible so they match the blank leaves of 7.5. The leaves are held near the flame rather than touching it, which is fine for this beat. Balloon space: the plain whitewash between his hair and the niche (upper right of centre), or the top of the window area at upper left.

Minor only: Ramayyan stands two or three paces back rather than one, and the fire lights his face less than Nagoji's. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud, topknot with grey at the temples, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain and buckled boots. Ramayyan matches too: receding curly hair, plain white cloth, barefoot. The room matches 7.5, 8.1, 8.3 and 8.4: barred window with rain and the neem behind, lamp niche in the side wall, low table with palm-leaf bundles, stools and the door. Both hands are sound, there is no text and no gore. The panel has no lettering.

Acceptable. The camera sits low at floor level. Papery grey-black palm-leaf ash, some flakes with orange edges, drifts down and lies scattered on the dark flagstones around Nagoji's buckled riding boots, with white breeches above them. The gravel heap is gone. The room plan matches 7.5: door and rush stool at left, rainy barred window, seat and table with bundles, and the lit niche on the right wall. Minor: the niche lamp is a brass bowl (as in 7.5), while 8.1 and 8.2 show clay, and the boots stand a little out from the niche. Balloon space is tight in the upper wall. Use the plain wall and the top of the open doorway at upper left, between the door and the window, and the dark, low-detail floor across the lower left for the second balloon. Nagoji is off-panel above, so both tails point up between the boots.

Acceptable. Ramayyan stands with empty hands, turned toward the niche, eyes lifted to the last orange spark on a curl of black ash beside the clay lamp, with a thread of smoke still hanging. The smile is open and warm: cheeks lifted, eyes crinkled, brows raised, lips just parted. Only a sliver of teeth shows, so it does not read as baring teeth, and it is clearly unlike his earlier thin, dry smiles. His likeness, plain white cloth, the rainy barred window and the table of untouched bundles all match. Minor: the niche is drawn as a deep rectangular recess, not the arched niche of 7.5, 8.2 and 8.3, and the door sits on the left wall. Caption space: the plain grey wall between the door and the window at upper left, and the wall between his head and the niche at upper right.

Usable, but with small misses. (1) The script asks for smoke still hanging between the two men, and none is drawn. The table holds neat bundles with no burnt remains, though this matches 8.4, which also shows no smoke. (2) The brand on the forearm is a small dark inked curl. Close up it looks like a glyph, not a pale puckered patch. At print size it is tiny, so soften it in retouch if possible. Otherwise it passes: Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, curled moustache, a small gold stud on the lobe, topknot with grey at the temples, the full uniform and the silver chain. Ramayyan matches his sheet. The room is right: rainy barred window, neem tree, lamp niche, closed door behind Nagoji. Plenty of plain wall between and above the heads for the four balloons.

The echo of Chapter 1 panel 1.2 is loose. This is an eye-level three-quarter view with the hands coming in from the left. The Chapter 1 frame is a high angle with the hand coming in from the right. Otherwise clean. The leaf carries only two scored strokes and no script. Both hands are sound: the stylus grip and the left hand guiding it. Ramayyan's plain white cloth shows at the shoulder. The room matches the page: lamp niche, rainy barred window, neem tree. Plain wall at top centre, roughly x 0.45 to 0.68 and y 0 to 0.45, takes the leaf caption.

Minor: the small leaf reads slightly like a wooden tablet, and the stylus on the table looks a little like a metal-tipped pen. Neither breaks the beat. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter row: curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Ramayyan holds up the leaf with its two scored lines, open to Nagoji, which matches 9.2 and 9.3. The leaf has no text. The room layout (door behind Nagoji's stool, barred window, niche lamp, rain outside) matches 9.5. Balloon space: upper wall between Nagoji's head and the window, and the top of the door or window.

Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, no marks. He draws a dark, worn bundle tied with faded cord out of an open wooden box, with sound hands. The room matches the others: barred window with rain, niche lamp, clay lamp on the table. There is no text. A large clear wall area at upper centre-right takes the long balloon.

In the foreground we see the back of Nagoji's head and shoulders: topknot, grey at the temple, a flush gold stud, the tip of his moustache, white coat, red collar and silver chain. Ramayyan faces him, flat and steady, holding the old tied bundle in both hands. The room is the same as in panels 9.3 and 9.4 (door at left, barred window with rain, niche lamp). There is no text. Balloon space: the upper wall right of Ramayyan's head, the upper door at left, and the top of the window or the wall below it. Nagoji's back-of-head entry in faces marks the foreground head so balloons stay off it.

Minor: a faint hatched shadow under the lower lip and on the chin reads as slight texture, but the chin is clean-shaven overall. The top of the topknot is cropped by the frame. Struck close-up matches the beat: thick curled moustache, grey at the temples, flush gold ear stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain, lamp niche on the left as in 10.5. The upper-right wall is clear for the balloon. No painted text.

Clean. Duarte matches his sheet: swept grey hair, a black cassock with a standing collar and no white tab, a small gold cross and the ink-stained fingers. He looks no younger than the sheet, which is acceptable. The trader matches the script: white skullcap, plain white cotton, clean-shaven, no scar, no coat or vest, so he cannot be read as Ibrahim. The sealed packet has no writing on it, the hands are sound and the palette is a muted night. The open night sky at upper right leaves room for both off-panel Ramayyan balloons.

Redrawn rather than the reused ch1 8.3 frame, but it follows the fallback description: a high vault view, small figures, the stool, the brazier, João's broad back with the bearded face from his sheet, leather jerkin and key ring, and Duarte standing apart in a black cassock with a standing collar, no white tab and a small cross. Young Nagoji wears ochre rags, bandaged wrists and ankle irons, with a moustache, a clean chin and an ear stud. The rope hangs plain from the iron ring with a frayed end, so there is no noose, and there is no gore. Minor: Duarte is grey-haired as on his sheet, where the memory-bleed note asked for darker hair. Muted palette apart from the brazier. The dark upper wall on both sides of the rope is free for the two off-panel balloons.

Acceptable, with minor points. The plain white flag on the bastion could be read as a flag of truce. The local gunners also wear white coats, so the European deserters are told apart only by their fair hair and beards. Otherwise it matches the beat: a dry, bright drill ground cut away with the same soft white edges, European instructors drilling local gunners at a bronze field gun, sound hands, no text and no anachronism. The large open sky across the top takes all three off-panel balloons.

Minor: a small beaded tie in the topknot, and his gaze is lifted upward rather than straight ahead, though it still reads as looking at nothing. Nagoji sits alone on the low stool with the door behind him and the niche lamp glowing beside him. This matches the room plan and panel 10.1: white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, topknot with grey temples, clean chin, flush ear stud, and the forearm scar on his left forearm. Hands are sound. The large plain wall on the right half gives ample room for both captions. No painted text.

Clean.
